name: Microsoft GraphRAG
ontology_notes: Indexer extracts entities, relationships, and claims from TextUnits, then Leiden communities and community reports. Query modes local, global, DRIFT, basic vector. The graph is a private corpus, not a companion. No user vs character vs relationship types.

ontology.evidence: docs/index.md: TextUnits, entities, relationships, claims, Leiden communities, community reports. Entity types come from indexing prompts. RAI_TRANSPARENCY.md intended use is private dataset Q&A.
ontology.label: measured

write_policy.evidence: Batch index over a corpus. LLM extracts entities/relations/claims then summarizes communities. Not a per-turn chat writer. Prompt tuning guide is required for domain-specific concepts.
write_policy.label: measured

read_policy.evidence: docs/query/overview.md: Local Search (entity-focused graph plus chunks), Global Search (map-reduce over community reports), DRIFT Search, Basic Search (vector RAG), Question Generation. The answer LLM always sees retrieved context.
read_policy.label: measured

supersession.evidence: README: re-index or run a migration notebook between versions. No incremental fact invalidation. Changing a document means another expensive index.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: No validity windows. Global questions are thematic over the whole corpus, not last Tuesday in a relationship.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: One indexed corpus. People/places/organizations in the data become entities. There is no user_id vs character vs relationship store.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Search returns relevant entities and community reports. No social skip.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: RAI_TRANSPARENCY.md: evaluated prompt injection and data attacks. Designed for trusted, trained analysts. Retrieved context is still model-readable text. LLM may produce offensive content.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: No user forget-that. Removing knowledge means editing the corpus and re-indexing.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: README warns indexing is expensive. Global search is map-reduce over community reports (many LLM calls per question). Local search is cheaper but still LLM-on-context. Start small.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: MIT. Runnable locally with an LLM. Indexing cost and model choice dominate. No vendor memory API required.
local.label: measured

mcp.evidence: README and docs/query/overview.md describe CLI and Python query engine. No official MCP server.
mcp.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: GraphRAG is corpus Q&A in maintenance mode. Community reports cannot split user vs character vs relationship. Indexing is a batch job, not a companion write policy. Cargo-culting it into roleplay mixes lore and chat into one expensive graph.

published_eval.name: GraphRAG paper arXiv 2404.16130 plus RAI evaluations
published_eval.claimed_score: Paper claims substantial improvement over baseline vector RAG on global/thematic questions over private corpora. RAI_TRANSPARENCY.md: gold-answer tests, groundedness, injection resilience, hallucination claim coverage. No LoCoMo number.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Dataset-level question answering and responsible-AI checks on a private corpus. Not companion memory.

open_unknowns: Numeric comprehensiveness/diversity tables from the 2024 blog vs current maintenance-mode code.
